jobs.description_text: OUR MISSION SPAN develops products that accelerate the rapid adoption of renewable energy in the home. The flagship SPAN Smart Panel is the first true evolution for the traditional home electric panel, harnessing enhanced technology for metering, monitoring, and control. An expanded product suite of intelligent, integrated solutions radically lowers the cost and complexity of energy upgrades–including solar, batteries and EVs–empowering homeowners to be active, resilient and informed players in the energy market. THE TEAM AND ROLE SPAN's Device Software team is responsible for all of the software that is physically embodied in our hardware products. The Gen3 SPAN Panel is a distributed system of STM32H5 (Arm Cortex-M33) microcontroller modules that talk over CAN, meter power in real time, and open or close relays that sit directly between the grid, the home and its solar, battery and EV equipment. When that firmware makes a decision, real current moves. We are building a dedicated Functional Safety (FuSa) firmware capability to take Gen3 firmware through certification as a Power Control System under UL 3141 and as Class B control software under UL/IEC 60730-1 Annex H. This is not a checkbox exercise: FuSa at SPAN spans how we architect and partition the firmware, how we detect faults and drive the system into defined safe states, how we test and prove coverage, and how we document and trace every safety requirement back to code. jobs.title: Member of the Technical Staff - Product Engineer
jobs.description_text: The Problem We’re Solving: A home’s survival in a wildfire or flood depends on its materials, geometry, topography, and defensible space. Traditional insurance models flatten that complexity, offering little insight to homeowners and few incentives for mitigation. Stand combines deterministic catastrophe models with modern AI to compute property-level risk and embed it directly into underwriting, pricing, and mitigation workflows. Instead of obscuring risk behind averages, we make it measurable and actionable - giving insurers sharper pricing signals and homeowners clear insight and incentives to mitigate. We build production software that connects scientific modeling to real-world insurance operations, turning physics into decisions. The Role: We’re hiring a Member of the Technical Staff - Product Engineer with engineering excellence - someone who has owned large product surfaces, navigated tradeoffs, and is comfortable being accountable for outcomes, not just implementations. This role is not narrowly scoped. You’ll own critical systems across the insurance lifecycle, from core workflows (policy, underwriting, claims, payments) to entirely new products like wildfire preparedness inspections, risk monitoring, and customer-facing mitigation tools. You’ll work closely with applied scientists, product leaders, and stakeholders to: - Translate complex domain problems into shippable systems - Decide what to build, not just how to build it - Productize models, pipelines, and tools

jobs.title: Head of Catastrophe and Emergency Response
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Stand is a homeowners insurance carrier for people who live where wildfire and hurricanes are a fact of life. The promise we make them is unusual: we try to reach you before the loss and get you help, and we handle the claim fast when it comes. This role owns both ends of that promise. Right now there is no single person who owns catastrophe readiness and response across Stand. Someone has to build the plan before a season, hold our claims partners to a real standard every day, and then run the whole thing when an event is bearing down on our customers. Without that, the promise is a slogan; with it, it's something a homeowner can count on. Concretely, the job is three things. You build and keep current the catastrophe plan, covering activation levels, who does what, vendor capacity, regulatory reporting, and how we reach customers and brokers. You manage the third-party administrators who handle our claims, day to day and against their service standards. And you own the Emergency Response Program: the work that finds policyholders in the path of an event and gets them help, increasingly automated, with people kept in the loop for the judgment calls. You report to the Head of Claims and Client Experience and work across the company. You'd partner with Product and Engineering on the automation, with Underwriting and the market teams on where our exposure sits, and with our TPAs and field vendors every week. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE We’re looking for a Software Engineer, Postgres Tooling to join our CLI team and help build the open-source tools developers use to change their Postgres schemas safely. You’ll join as a co-maintainer of pg-delta, our schema diff and migration engine, and grow into leading it. Given two databases, or a database and a folder of SQL files describing the schema you want, pg-delta works out the differences and generates the migration to get from one to the other. It powers supabase db diff, db pull, and declarative schemas, and it runs underneath Supabase’s platform, branching, and AI agent workflows. Every migration it generates is verified on a throwaway clone before it’s trusted, and it’s tested against 331 scenarios on PostgreSQL 14–18. We’re now working toward a stable, standalone 1.0 release for any Postgres developer, on Supabase or not. This is a correctness-first role. The SQL this tool generates runs against production databases, so privilege safety and avoiding data loss are non-negotiable. It’s a great fit for someone who loves Postgres at the catalog level, enjoys compiler-style problems, and thrives in async, fast-paced environments. WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR In this role, you’ll: - Co-maintain pg-delta: review and merge changes, including PRs written by AI agents, and grow into its lead maintainer. - Own correctness: triage bug reports from GitHub and support, fix diff and dependency-ordering bugs, and extend test coverage across Postgres versio

As an Electrical Engineer, you will design, bring up, test, and refine the electronics that let our camera modules, gimbals, and imaging payloads perform reliably in the field. You will take ownership of circuits and boards, from schematic through bring-up and into production. As drone programs move from the age of tools to the age of infrastructure, we are expanding our public safety sales team to meet that demand. About the role: As a Key Account Director, Corrections at Skydio, you will lead a national team of Key Account Leaders selling into State Departments of Corrections and state-funded Port Authorities. This is a first-line leadership role, and the job comes down to three things: recruiting the right people, coaching them into great sellers, and keeping them here. You will not carry your own accounts. Your number is your team’s number, and you will hit it by making each person on the team better: sharpening deal strategy, getting into the field on their most competitive pursuits, and building the territory, pipeline, and forecast discipline that makes a segment predictable. You will work alongside peer Directors leading other segments and geographies, and across Channel, Sales Engineering, Business Development, Marketing, Strategic Relationships, Government Relations, and Mission Success. Corrections is one of our least penetrated markets, so building the Skydio brand with DOC leadership is part of the job alongside building the team. You will also set the standard for how the team works, not only what it sells.

jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Skydio is seeking an experienced physical security professional to join our team as Solutions Engineer – Commercial Site Security. Commercial Solutions Engineering is the technical arm of Skydio's commercial go-to-market motion. We sit between the customer and the product: translating industrial and security problems into deployable programs, proving capability in the field, and making sure Skydio's products are integrated and flown at scale across sites that were never designed with drones in mind. Coverage is tiered by customer size rather than by territory, so the team is measured on technical win rate, trial and proof of concept outcomes, program expansion inside existing accounts, and the requirements we push back into the product organization. Solutions Engineers are critical members of the Skydio organization and work closely with Account Executives, Engineering, and Product to support deal progression, customer confidence, successful deployments, and the long-term success of commercial sUAS programs.
